findings.quote: Copilot Money charges $9 per month, or $109 billed yearly as a limited-time offer down from $119.
findings.problem: copilot.money/pricing publishes '$9 per month' with '$109 billed yearly, instead of $119' on one yearly view and no separate monthly-billed price (WebFetch confirmed). The page presents $9 as a monthly-billing plan and builds comparisons on it: 'twelve monthly payments of $9 ($108 total)', 'Copilot Money charges a lower monthly fee ($9 versus $14.99)', EveryDollar '$107.88 more than 12 months of Copilot Money at $9', YNAB '$70.88' monthly difference, FAQ 'costs $9 per month'. Also the $119 is 'instead of' wording, not a labelled regular price ('regular $119 price', '$119 versus $109' scenarios).
findings.fix: Restate as '$109 billed yearly (limited-time, listed instead of $119); the page shows $9 per month as the yearly-billing equivalent and publishes no monthly-billing price'. Delete every $108/12x$9/'lower monthly fee' calculation in the table, chooseSection, Monarch, YNAB, EveryDollar sections, verdict, FAQs and 'Would Change Our Answer'.

findings.quote: Who This Is Not For: This comparison focuses on consumer personal budgeting and spending applications.
findings.problem: Section opens with a stub sentence plus blank paragraphs; the only substantive sentence also claims Copilot, Monarch, YNAB and Tiller 'all require paid subscriptions to maintain automatic bank connections', which is unsourced (trial and refund terms differ; no source states bank-sync gating).
findings.fix: Replace with sourced bullets; remove blank paragraphs and unsourced absolute claim.

findings.fix: Limit to what the vendor's page lists ('Tiller's pricing page lists no money assistant') or remove.
